name: The Pleated Nave

detectability.signature: Regular banded distortion like corrugated glass; lidar returns arrive out of launch order

proximity: The starfield appears combed into parallel ridges of compressed light
Navigation instruments give contradictory range readings fore and aft
contact: Ship length appears to triple to outside observers while the crew measures no change
Crossing a fold ridge produces a brief sensation of falling sideways
prolonged_exposure: Crew develop persistent double vision and mild vertigo
Structural fasteners loosen as the hull is repeatedly micro-folded

phenomena: Objects appearing larger or smaller than they are
Visible distortion of starfield in regular bands
hazards: Progressive hull fatigue from repeated fold cycling
known_incidents: Fold-liner packets routed through the nave cut six weeks off the Delve Run until toll disputes closed the route in 2398
A pleasure yacht misjudged a ridge and arrived folded a meter shorter; her passengers survived and sued
description: Space within the Pleated Nave is gathered into immense, regular folds, like a curtain of dressed stone drawn shut across a fortieth of an astronomical unit. From a distance the region resembles corrugated crystal: bands of compressed starlight alternating with bands of unnatural black gap. Survey buoys confirm the ridges are genuine gradients in distance itself, not optical artifacts.

The structure is perfectly still, holding its arrangement within instrument error for over two centuries of observation. Ships riding a fold ridge travel folded distances and emerge far along the nave's axis, which made it a celebrated shortcut in its early years. Crews who linger report their own reflections lagging a half-beat behind their movements.

Its geometric regularity betrays artificial manufacture, and xenotechnicians date construction to roughly two centuries ago by a builder unknown. Toll convoys ran the ridges for decades until a legal feud between rival anchorages sealed the route. Academic interest has since outpaced commerce, folding studies being what they are.

The nave remains open but poorly patrolled, its entrances marked by warning buoys blinking patient sequences. Engineers continue to argue whether removing a single ridge would unravel the whole structure. Smugglers who still know the ridge lines guard them like guild secrets.
